newsitem.title: UK: Matthew Clark premium brands off 30 percent.
newsitem.headline: Matthew Clark premium brands off 30 percent.

text.p: Cider maker Matthew Clark said sales of its premium packaged brands, Diamond White, K and Babycham fell 30 percent in the first five months of this financial year as a result of the unprecedented growth in alcopops in the summer and price competition.
Matthew Clark is a bigger player than its rival, HP Bulmer, at the premium end of the market, so the impact of alcopops on its business has been more severe.
The competitive pricing pressures have continued, said the company and in June and July, sales of draught cider were down 10 percent compared with last year's hot summer.

The group's draught cider sales were down 15 percent across the whole summer but current trading in cider has stabilised after the summer's severe trading environment, the company said. "We expect the underlying growth within the cider market as a whole to resume," it said.
The company said it expects to maintain its interim dividend, with the results for the half year ending October 31.

Matthew Clark, stunned the stockmarket in September with a profits warning that wiped more than 290 million stg off its market value. Since then the shares have held up at about 60 percent below their pre-warning September 9 price of 670p.

The shares rose 15p to 318p amid relief that the dividend at the half year may be held at 9.0p. "The thing that's made them bounce is they've said they expect to maintain the dividend. But you've got to be cautious because there's no guide as to underlying profit levels," said one dealer.

When the adverse trading became evident, the company initiated a review of its marketing strategy in branded drinks -- mainly Diamond White and mainstream ciders Dry Blacthorn and Gaymers Olde English. The key findings of the review will be made public in January, said Matthew Clark.
In the meantime, the company said it will create the new position of marketing director, a main board appointment and take on 40 more staff in sales and marketing in its branded drinks division.
The company said the transfer of its bottling from Taunton, in south west England, will be completed by the end of 1996 but would mean the loss of 45 jobs.
Alcopops -- alcholic lemonades and similar long alcoholic drinks -- have proved especially popular with young drinkers, forging major inroads into the British drinks market.
In May, research body Euromonitor saId it would be worth about 170 million stg this year after 100 million in 1995.
Leading lines include alcoholic lemonade Hooper's Hooch, owned by Bass and Two Dogs, marketed by Merrydown.
Drinks industry leaders agreed in January to a voluntary code of practice aimed at avoiding promotion of alcopops to underage drinkers.
In its last budget the government imposed a heavy duty on ciders with an alcohol content over 7.5 percent from next year but left alcoholic colas and lemonades unaffected.
